text: A quagmire is literally boggy ground that swallows your feet. Figuratively it is a messy situation, often a war, that is hard to escape and gets worse the harder you struggle. Here the Economist says Saudi Arabia's war in Yemen had already become one years ago.

A putsch is a sudden, planned attempt by a small group to overthrow a government by force. The word is German. Here the Economist means that no rival of the crown prince is strong enough to try to remove him.

A façade is the front face of a building, and figuratively an outward appearance that may hide a different reality. The Economist says Saudi social reforms are real, but the deeper foundations of the state have not changed.
Latin for 'horrible year', used for a year when one disaster follows another. Queen Elizabeth II made the phrase famous in 1992. Here it describes the crown prince's run of crises.
Glad-handing means greeting and charming people warmly, often to win favour or business. The crown prince usually spends the summit week doing this with leaders and financiers.
In Greek myth the Titans were giant gods. Today a titan of an industry is a hugely powerful figure in it, so 'titans of finance' means the biggest names in banking and investing.
Dignitaries are people of high rank or office, such as ministers and ambassadors, who attend important events.

Davos is the Swiss town that hosts the World Economic Forum, a yearly gathering of the world's political and business leaders. Calling the Saudi summit 'Davos in the desert' says it is the Gulf's version of that meeting.
A yearly business conference in Riyadh where Saudi Arabia courts foreign investors and announces deals. Postponing it is a visible sign of how unsafe the capital has felt.
A Yemeni armed movement that controls much of northern Yemen and is backed by Iran. It has fought a Saudi-led coalition since 2015 and now fires missiles and drones at Saudi cities.
An armed group that is not part of a country's regular army. Militias often fight for a cause, a region or a sponsoring state.
If something is emblematic of a situation, it stands as a clear symbol of it. Cancelling the summit shows, in one event, how badly the year has gone.
Interlocking things fit together like gears, so that each affects the others. Interlocking crises cannot be solved one at a time.
A 'ready' solution is one that is available right now, with no further work needed. The article says none of the prince's crises has one.
A truce is an agreement to stop fighting for a time. It is weaker than a peace treaty, and the one agreed in 2022 has now begun to fall apart.
To unravel is to come apart thread by thread, like a knitted sweater. A truce that unravels weakens bit by bit until the fighting returns.
Here 'cement' is a verb meaning to make something firm and permanent, as cement does when it sets. Making a deal that helps cement Houthi rule would lock in their control.
Attacks carried out by aircraft dropping bombs or firing missiles. They can damage targets from the sky but rarely win control of territory by themselves.
To derail is to make a train leave its tracks, and figuratively to knock a plan off course. A long war could derail the crown prince's economic programme.
Sputtering describes an engine that coughs and stalls. A sputtering economic programme is one making weak, uneven progress.
To shelve a project is to put it aside, as if on a shelf, and stop work on it, often indefinitely.
A strain on finances is heavy pressure that makes it hard to pay for everything. It does not mean a type, as in a strain of virus.
The government's income from taxes and oil, set against what it spends. When they are strained, the state has to cut or delay spending.
Money from abroad used to build or buy something lasting inside a country, such as a factory. Saudi Arabia gets only about a third of its $100bn yearly target.
The International Monetary Fund, a global body of 190 countries that lends to governments in trouble and publishes forecasts for national economies.
Here, a contraction is an economy getting smaller rather than growing. The IMF now expects Saudi output to shrink 3.3% in 2026.
To rebound is to bounce back after a fall, as a basketball does off the backboard. An economy that rebounds grows again after shrinking.
To woo someone is to try to win their favour with flattery or gifts, a word first used for courting a romantic partner.
Hard to believe because it seems unlikely. 'Implausible sums' are amounts so large that nobody expects them to be paid in full.
Showy but cheap and morally shabby. Calling the deals tawdry suggests they looked like favours for the president's family rather than ordinary business.
The family of a country's president. Deals with the 'first family' mean business with the president's own relatives.
The husband of one's daughter. Jared Kushner, who married Donald Trump's daughter Ivanka, got $2bn from Saudi investors.
To embark is to start a journey or big undertaking, from boarding a ship. 'Embarking on a war' means starting one.
Making someone anxious or shaken, as if their nerve were draining away.
Something interrupting normal life, here travel, business and daily routines.
Exaggerated, made to sound more serious than it really is.
An heir is someone who will inherit a position, here the throne. Prince Muhammad was a newly appointed heir, the crown prince who was to succeed the king.
To make something stronger and more secure by combining and tightening it. A ruler who consolidates power gathers it into his own hands.
Cutting a country off by force, closing its borders, ports or airspace so goods and people cannot pass. Saudi Arabia and neighbours blockaded Qatar from 2017 to 2021.
A Saudi journalist and critic of the crown prince, murdered in 2018 inside the Saudi consulate in Istanbul. His killing made Prince Muhammad an outcast in much of the West.
Pushed out of the centre of action, like a player benched during a game. The prince removed rivals from real power.
Gathered into one place. Centralised power means decisions that once belonged to many people are made by one.
Abdulaziz ibn Saud, who united the territories into the modern kingdom of Saudi Arabia in 1932. His sons have ruled since, and Prince Muhammad is his grandson.
People who criticise someone or try to reduce their reputation.
Done unwillingly, with reluctance. The Biden administration only reluctantly praised the prince's change of course.
A pariah is an outcast whom others avoid. The word comes from a Tamil name for a social group. Biden promised to treat the prince as one.
Practical and focused on what works, not on ideals or pride.
Missiles fired to hit and destroy incoming missiles or drones. Each one used up is hard to replace quickly.
US elections held halfway through a president's four-year term, when voters choose all of the House of Representatives and a third of the Senate.
Deserving praise. The word shares a root with 'applaud'.
Strides are long steps, and 'make strides' means to make quick, noticeable progress.
German for 'forbidden', used in English for something strictly not allowed. Cinemas and concerts were long banned in Saudi Arabia.
A British, slightly playful word for an alcoholic drink. Alcohol is tightly banned in Saudi Arabia, so a 'legal tipple' is a notable change.
To take the place of something, often by pushing it out. New allies that supplant America would replace it as protector.
A mutual-defence agreement between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey.
A treaty in which countries promise to help defend one another if any is attacked. NATO is the best-known example.
